name: Tungsten
occurrence: Mined from wolframite and scheelite ores; its chemical symbol W comes from 'wolfram', its older German name.
majorUses: Cutting tools and drill bits (tungsten carbide, extremely hard)
notableCharacteristics: Has the highest melting point of any metal on the periodic table, which is exactly why it was the standard filament material in incandescent bulbs for over a century.
ncertRelevance: highest melting point of any metal
whyHere: Its six valence electrons across 5d and 6s orbitals support unusually strong metallic bonding throughout the lattice, which directly explains both tungsten's record-setting melting point and its extreme hardness in carbide form.
didYouKnow: Tungsten's chemical symbol W has nothing to do with its English name — it comes from 'wolfram', an older German name referencing how the mineral wolframite was said to 'eat' tin like a wolf during smelting.
genZNote: Highest melting point of any metal, period. Also has a symbol that doesn't match its name because German miners blamed a wolf.
